notes:
Lead source: inbound - signed up for free credits, ran quick smoke tests. Small engineering org (mobile-first SaaS). Primary contact: CTO - Leo Martens; Product lead: Saanvi Rao.

Summary of ask: wants Hosted API (self-serve) but strict rules on prompt and log retention. Concerned about storing customer prompts and PII that flows through conversational support agents.

Key constraints / asks (verbatim & paraphrase):
- "We need an easy way to opt-out of prompt retention for specific customers" (CTO).
- default retention window they'd accept: 30-90 days depending on data classification.
- Legal requests: sample DPA text stating no storage of user prompts beyond retention window; audit trail of access; KMS usage for keys in transit.
- Engineering: wants API header to flag 'no-store' so Redwood doesn't persist KV/prefix caches for those requests. Also asked about ability to anonymize logs on ingest (hashing/email redaction).

Timeline / activities (recent):
- 2026-02-12: Account created via self-serve signup; used free tier credits for embedding tests.
- 2026-02-20: Intro call (Avery Chen) - high level product fit, confirmed public cloud ok. Fireflies: ff_20260301_1123 (transcript + recording).
- 2026-02-26: Short technical sync with SE Maya Patel - demo of hosted API, shown streaming and function-calling. SE noted: need to verify delete API for user content.
- 2026-03-03: Legal sent initial checklist asking for retention policy, whether prompts used for model training, and sample DPA clause.
- 2026-03-05: Follow-up call - CTO reiterated: "we can't have free-form prompt logs retained indefinitely; customers must be able to opt-out."

Product notes (what they care about):
- Prefer Hosted API (fast time-to-value) but must have explicit opt-out for prompt storage and short log retention window.
- Cost sensitivity: token-level billing OK, but storing logs for long periods increases bill; want option to purge or archive to customer-owned S3.
- Routing/fallback: occasional routing to cheaper model for low-sensitivity traffic acceptable, but strict policy for high-sensitivity tenants.

Questions they asked that need answers:
- Can Redwood support request-level 'no-store' header? If yes, how is it reflected in billing/metrics?
- Is there a self-service retention slider in Console (30 / 90 / 180 / custom)?
- Where are logs retained (region)? Can we pin retention per-organization?
- Are prompts ever used for model training or evaluation by Redwood?
- Support for purge API + proof of deletion (audit log) for compliance.

Next steps (practical):
- Send tailored security FAQ + sample DPA clause (Avery) - due 2026-03-12 (in flight).
- SE (Maya) to run internal check with infra on feasibility of 'no-store' header and per-tenant retention settings; estimate by 2026-03-17.
- Offer 30-day default retention pilot and confirm if customer will accept paid add-on for storing logs in their own S3 (to satisfy residency).

Notes tone: choppy CRM style, fragments, some direct quote bits. Customer enthusiastic about product but very risk-averse on data retention.
